title: How do you find and fix N+1 query patterns?
description: The query-per-row trap in ORMs and hand-written code: spotting it in logs and traces, fixing with joins/projection/batching, and when N+1 is fine.

data.text: **Question:** How do you find and fix N+1 query patterns?

An N+1 happens when you fetch a list (1 query) and then run **another query per row** (N queries) — usually a lazy-loaded navigation property or a per-item lookup in a loop. It's invisible in dev with 3 rows and catastrophic in prod with 500: latency becomes N round trips (~5ms each locally, 30–100ms over a network). **Find it**: count queries per request in logs/MiniProfiler/tracing spans — 200 queries for one page is the signature; enable EF Core's lazy-loading warnings and log every command in dev. **Fix it**: eager-load with `Include`/projection, batch the lookups into one `WHERE Id IN (...)`, or use a dataloader pattern to coalesce concurrent requests. Not every N+1 is wrong — small N with warm local DB may be simpler and just as fast; the sin is discovering it at 10× data volume.

items: Classic sources: lazy-loaded navigation in a loop (EF Core .Include missing), per-row permission lookups, per-row tax/shipping calls, serializers touching unloaded properties
Detection tools: MiniProfiler (query list per request), EF Core logging ('Executed DbCommand'), distributed tracing spans (one span per query), and simply logging query count per request
Fix 1 — Include/projection: one JOINed query; project to a DTO so you don't drag entity graphs
Fix 2 — batch: collect ids in the loop, one WHERE Id IN (...) or a VALUES-join for huge sets
Fix 3 — dataloader: coalesce concurrent per-key fetches (GraphQL dataloaders, or manual batching) — great for per-user lookups under parallel load
Watch the fix's shape: Include of a filtered collection (Where inside Include) can produce row multiplication — use filtered Include or projection
DTO projection beats Include for read paths: less data, no tracking overhead, no accidental lazy loads later
Not always bad: N ≤ ~10 on a local DB, or when queries hit different shards intentionally — measure, don't dogma

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: N+1 = 1 list query + one query per row; latency = N network round trips
Detect via query counts: MiniProfiler, EF logs, trace spans
Fix: project (one JOINed query), batch WHERE IN, or dataloader coalescing
Filtered Includes multiply rows — split or project instead
data.takeaway: The query log never lies: if one page issues a query count proportional to its row count, you've found the N+1 — fix it with one round trip, not cleverer loops.
